anatomy.flutter: ToggleGroup builds one ActiveIndicator(indicator: Surface(bg-primary, shadow-chip-equivalent)) whose children are Toggle(inExclusiveGroup: true) items, wrapped in SingleChildScrollView and optionally Semantics(container:true, label) — the travelling pill plus a row of Toggle items.
anatomy.web: ToggleGroupPrimitive.Root renders <ActiveIndicator indicatorRef .../> as its first child followed by ToggleGroupContext.Provider wrapping ToggleGroupItem children — the doc comment confirms 'the group renders as its first child' matching ActiveIndicator's paint-first placement in Flutter.

api.flutter: ToggleGroup(items: List<ToggleGroupItem>{label,child,enabled,disabledReason}, selectedIndex: int?, onChanged: ValueChanged<int?>, variant, size, label) — no spacing parameter and no orientation parameter anywhere on the widget.
api.web: ToggleGroup({className, variant, size, spacing = 2, orientation = 'horizontal' | 'vertical', ...ToggleGroupPrimitive.Root props}) — spacing drives '--gap' inline and a whole bordered-segmented-control class branch (data-[spacing=0]:rounded-none, first/last corner rounding, collapsed inner borders) and orientation drives data-vertical:flex-col.
api.note: RE-EXAMINED after a review listed toggle-group keyboard/API differences as open. Read against the Dart source: toggle_group.dart L141-145: "Two props of the reference's root are not ported. `spacing` (default 2) and `orientation` (default horizontal) each select a whole dormant branch of the item's class list." The web is the reference here and has all three — `spacing`, `orientation`, and one Tab stop with arrow keys via Radix's roving focus group, which is the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern. Matching Flutter would mean giving every toggle its own Tab stop, which is a regression to a shortfall Flutter itself calls a divergence. Kept as the web behaviour; the page's Keyboard section states the difference. ORIGINAL: toggle_group.dart's own doc states this outright: 'Two props of the reference's root are not ported. spacing (default 2) and orientation (default horizontal) each select a whole dormant branch of the item's class list... The page passes neither, no #api row prints them, and a parameter that silently did nothing would be worse than an absent one. They are recorded here instead.' So a caller cannot get the web's spacing=0 bordered-segmented look or a vertical group from the Flutter widget at all — a real, documented capability gap rather than a defect nobody noticed.

states.flutter: Toggle items composed with pressedFill: transparent, pressedInk: theme.primaryForeground reproduce the doc's own resolved state table: rest unselected = no fill/--foreground ink, hover unselected = --muted/--foreground, selected = transparent (pill shows through)/--primary-foreground, focus-visible = a 3px ring at --ring @50%.
states.web: ToggleGroupItem's class list appends 'data-[state=on]:bg-transparent data-[state=on]:text-primary-foreground' AFTER toggleVariants(...) specifically so the selected item's own background gives way to the travelling pill underneath, per the file's own comment about tailwind-merge ordering.

disabled.flutter: ToggleGroupItem.enabled (default true) gates onChanged: items[i].enabled ? (bool on) => onChanged(...) : null, and disabledReason is passed straight through to the underlying Toggle's disabledReason.
disabled.web: ToggleGroupPrimitive.Item forwards Radix's own disabled prop, which toggleVariants' base class styles with disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 — the doc notes neither side's disabled option is exercised on the live page but both declare the capability identically.

interaction.flutter: Flutter's traversal gives every ToggleGroupItem its own independent Tab stop — there is no shared focus-node/arrow-key wiring at the ToggleGroup level at all (unlike Tabs.dart's _onKey), so arrow keys do not move selection between options.
interaction.web: Radix wraps ToggleGroupPrimitive.Item children in a RovingFocusGroup: one Tab stop for the whole group, with arrow keys moving focus (and, for type="single", selection) between options.
interaction.note: RE-EXAMINED after a review listed toggle-group keyboard/API differences as open. Read against the Dart source: toggle_group.dart L150-154: "Roving focus is not ported either. Radix wraps the items in a RovingFocusGroup: one Tab stop for the whole group, arrow keys to move within it. Flutter's traversal gives every item its own Tab stop. Building half of a roving group … would be worse than the honest divergence." The web is the reference here and has all three — `spacing`, `orientation`, and one Tab stop with arrow keys via Radix's roving focus group, which is the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern. Matching Flutter would mean giving every toggle its own Tab stop, which is a regression to a shortfall Flutter itself calls a divergence. Kept as the web behaviour; the page's Keyboard section states the difference. ORIGINAL: toggle_group.dart's own doc says so directly: 'Roving focus is not ported either... Flutter's traversal gives every item its own Tab stop... Building half of a roving group — arrow keys without the single tab stop, or the reverse — would be worse than the honest divergence, so the divergence is stated rather than approximated.' This is a genuine interaction-model gap (a keyboard user tabs through N stops instead of one plus arrow keys), documented as a deliberate incompleteness rather than fixed.

semantics.flutter: Each item is a Toggle(inExclusiveGroup: true), so it reports Semantics(selected: pressed, inMutuallyExclusiveGroup: true) rather than a bare toggled boolean — 'one choice among others,' per toggle.dart's own doc, matching Radix's radio-shaped semantics for a single-select group.
semantics.web: ToggleGroupPrimitive.Item under Radix's type="single" gets radio-group-shaped ARIA semantics (a set of mutually exclusive options), so a screen reader announces the group's items as a set rather than as independent switches — the same distinction toggle_group.dart's doc draws.
